chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, and Hishām, and Ḥafṣ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
That some women entered upon him, and one woman among them asked him about siḥāq, so he said: “Its hadd is the hadd of the fornicator.”
So the woman said: “Allah has not mentioned that in the Qur’an.” He said: “Yes, indeed.” She said: “And where?”
He said: “They are the companions of al-Rass.”

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الرَّسِّ: the companions of al-Rass, cited here as the Qur'anic referent
key_terms.السِّحَاقِ: female same-sex sexual act mentioned in the legal question
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an as the source being discussed
key_terms.حَدُّ الزَّانِي: the legal punishment of the fornicator used here as the comparison

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith connect the ruling on siḥāq to the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning siḥāq and links it to a Qur'anic allusion through the mention of the companions of al-Rass. It also reflects an interpretive exchange in which the Imam عليه السلام affirms that the basis of the ruling is indicated in the Qur'an.
